prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1132; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a reported rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped. Police report requested. Insured reports neck stiffness and headache at scene; ambulance transported claimant to hospital for evaluation. Claimant is represented by counsel, who has requested all communications be routed through the firm.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and acknowledge letter of representation. Attorney indicated client has been diagnosed with a concussion and is under ongoing treatment. Requested copies of the police report, photographs of both vehicles, and the at-fault party's policy declarations page. Liability appears clear based on initial statements and scene evidence.

Entry 3: Received medical records from claimant's treating facility through counsel. Records document concussion diagnosis, follow-up with neurology, and restrictions on screen time and work activity. Treatment ongoing. Reviewed records for pre-existing conditions; none noted relevant to current complaints. Referred file to medical review for analysis of injury severity and expected recovery timeline.

Entry 4: Counsel's office contacted to request updated status and authorization to obtain additional records from primary care provider. Attorney stated client continues to experience headaches, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating, and that a demand package will follow once treatment reaches a stable point. Authorization forms sent for signature. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect ongoing treatment.

Entry 5: Medical review completed. Reviewer notes concussion symptoms consistent with mechanism of injury and recommends a neuropsychological evaluation before evaluating a settlement range. Advised counsel of this recommendation in writing. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days to check on the status of the evaluation and any demand submission.
